review_notes: I read the whole 96-line file. I also read the related definitions: CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient, mkQuotient_apply (not simp), quotientPointsHom_apply_apply (simp, and its RHS is stated with Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ), and baseChangeIsoPointsMulEquiv_apply_apply (simp). I did not run Lean, so I have not checked whether the proposed restatement compiles. The only finding is about the normal form of the private helper lemma. findings.problem: The helper lemma is stated with `(CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ _).hom`. The simp interface it feeds, `quotientPointsHom_apply_apply`, is a `@[simp]` lemma whose right-hand side is `f.ofConv (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I.toIdeal h)`. So the normal form after the first rewrite is `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ`, not `mkQuotient`. The main proof therefore has to rewrite backwards with `← CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_apply` twice, once per side, so the goal matches the helper. That moves the expression away from the simp normal form, only for `exact congrArg q.ofConv (...)` to match. The docstring admits the mismatch ("which `simp` unfolds to `Ideal.Quotient.mk`, so it is a `rw` lemma rather than a `simp` one"), and the helper cannot be used with the simp-normal output of the existing simp lemmas. The `mkQuotient_apply` rewrites are fragile bookkeeping: they depend on the exact `rw` order and on `mkQuotient` being an abbrev.
findings.proposed_change: Restate `iso_inv_one_tmul_mkQuotient_X` with `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ k I.toIdeal` and `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A J.toIdeal` in place of the `mkQuotient ... .hom` applications. That is the form produced by `quotientPointsHom_apply_apply`. Inside its proof, turn the statement into the `mkQuotient` form (via `CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_apply`) only where needed to use `he`. Then drop the two `← CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_apply` steps in the main theorem. The `rw [quotientPointsHom_apply_apply, quotientPointsHom_apply_apply, baseChangeIsoPointsMulEquiv_apply_apply]` and `exact congrArg q.ofConv ...` steps would then line up directly, or `simp only` with the two existing simp lemmas would suffice. The conversion to the categorical `mkQuotient` form stays inside the one lemma that needs `he`.
findings.benefit: The helper lemma is stated in the same normal form the library's simp lemmas produce. The main proof no longer needs forward-then-backward rewriting with `mkQuotient_apply`. The `rw` versus `simp` caveat in the docstring goes away. Later point-equivalence lemmas that end in `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ` can reuse the helper without first re-folding into `mkQuotient`.
